extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers of media criticism, communications, and cultural studies
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and evaluate staged or simulated public events, manufactured celebrity identities, and other ‘images’ that replace or obscure underlying reality in mass culture. Use Boorstin's concepts to diagnose the degree and effects of contrivance in public life and communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-events (staged and scripted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pseudo-events — staged and scripted events that are a kind of counterfeit version of actual happenings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as a criterion whether an occurrence is performed primarily for publicity/representation rather than arising organically. Examples include events created to be reported, press stunts, contrived spectacles; anti-patterns are treating reported coverage of a pseudo-event as if it documented an unmediated reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufactured celebrity identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeit people — celebrities — whose identities were being staged and scripted, to create illusions that often had no relationship to any underlying reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate public figures for the extent their persona is constructed by image-makers/PR rather than grounded in observable action or character. Look for scripting, repeated manufactured moments, and image-management practices that replace substantive biography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of contrivance vs. authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: America was living in an 'age of contrivance,' in which illusions and fabrications had become a dominant force in society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess communications for how much they replace authentic content, ideals, or factual basis with surface imagery. Score higher contrivance when the message prioritizes appearance, packaging, or spectacle over substantive connection to reality or ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging of politics and public figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The packaging of politicians, politics and celebrities — criticism of how public life is filled with pseudo-events and staged images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge political communications by how much they are crafted as marketable images (soundbites, staged encounters, photo opportunities) rather than conveying policy substance or accountability. Anti-patterns include prioritizing optics over policy, rehearsed interactions presented as spontaneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tourism and production of 'artificial products'
rubrics_metrics.description: Tourism... now insulated travelers from the places they were visiting, and, instead, provided 'artificial products,' in which 'picturesque natives fashion(ed) papier-mâché images of themselves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a rubric to evaluate representations of places/peoples: are portrayals simplified, commodified, or performed for outsiders rather than reflecting lived reality? Watch for curated experiences that substitute stereotyped images for complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of ideals by superficial images
rubrics_metrics.description: America was losing contact, not merely with reality, but with the ideals that had given the nation strength... American ideals were being replaced by superficial images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a message or cultural practice undermines or substitutes for underlying civic/cultural ideals. Higher concern when symbolic gestures substitute for substantive adherence to principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interconnectedness of simulated phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulation is a distinct social category, linking together many apparently disparate phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate communications in context across media and institutions — identify patterns where separate practices (celebrity culture, tourism, political PR) reinforce a broader simulated environment rather than isolated incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation: exploitation of desire for transcendence
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek simulations because we aren't satisfied with what the mundane, nonfiction, world can offer; simulations offer forms of phony transcendence over everyday life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether messages deliberately appeal to consumers' desire for escape or elevated experience, and whether they exploit that desire by offering symbolic or staged substitutes rather than substantive improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normative stance and ideological provenance of critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Boorstin's criticism came from the political right; it is in a long tradition of works that warn against the vulgarization of high culture by mass society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using Boorstin's framework, account for its ideological perspective — evaluate whether the critique privileges certain cultural ideals (e.g., 'high culture') and how that shapes judgments about mass-produced images. Use as a lens to interrogate both media practices and the values guiding their critique.
